evidence.note: rootOf parses only the first porcelain block and refuses a bare main worktree; strings.Split never returns an empty slice, so lines[0] cannot panic even on empty output, and err/code != 0 is already mapped to ERR_NOT_A_REPO.

scenarioFor is path-bound (RepoRoot equality) and resolves the mock dir with filepath.Join(root, rel) before relInside; machine/machine.go:163 stores Mock as a repo-relative path, so the Join cannot be subverted by an absolute stored value.

Verified kind.New's only error (CodeMockMismatch at internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:76) is unreachable here: judge.NewMock returns *judge.MockJudge and Mock is derived from the same scenario != nil test, so the discarded error is genuinely dead.

resolveRun's flag -> MRV_RUN_ID -> newest-without-error precedence is sound: run.sortSummaries (internal/fsm/run/store.go:220) sorts CreatedAt descending, so the first non-error summary really is the newest, and both flag and env paths run ValidateRunID before use.

applyJudgeOverrideFor copies the caller's vars map before mutation and drops only the environment (never the flag) under --calibration, matching the documented rationale that a flag is a real conflict Resolve must report.

TestCodexJudgeBuildsASafeInvocation pins the security-relevant argv: --sandbox read-only, --skip-git-repo-check, prompt on stdin via trailing '-', plus a negative assertion that the candidate text never reaches argv where the process table would expose it.
TestCodexJudgeReportsTokensEvenWhenTheCallFails matches codex.go:64-70, which assigns v.Tokens from parseCodexEvents before the exec/exit-code error branches, so usage survives a failed turn.

TestCodexPrefixStrippingMatchesRouting is a real regression test: route lowercases (judge.go:114) while wireModel now uses trimPrefixFold (judge.go:168-176), so mixed-case codex/ prefixes route and strip consistently.

TestPreflightSeam asserts the no-side-effect contract in both directions: a refusing Preflight at init creates no run (store.List empty), and a refusing Preflight at advance appends no event (store.appends unchanged).

TestRecordLLMCall covers the append-on-error case, the append-nothing-on-cancel case, terminal and torn refusals, and Lock/append failure passthrough; index monotonicity is asserted rather than assumed.
TestReadOnlyOpen pins that a read-only open ignores a held lock, a re-pinned binary hash and a missing mock scenario (loads == 0), while a full open still contends for the lock.

Validation run locally on the frozen branch: go test ./internal/fsm/cli/ ./internal/fsm/judge/ ./internal/fsm/machine/ passes, and go test -cover reports 100.0% of statements for all three packages. No TODO/FIXME markers, no eval-style dynamic execution, and no untracked source introduced by this shard.

findings.note: Duplicated containment guard: relInside is byte-for-byte identical in internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:103 and internal/fsm/machine/machine.go:228, and both copies enforce the same security-relevant rule that a mock scenario must live inside the repository. cli already imports machine, so one exported helper would do. Divergence risk only; today the two copies agree. The inline comment documents the invariant; propagating the error would cost one line.

findings.note: Misleading error text: resolveRun falls through to ERR_NO_RUNS with the message 'no FSM runs in this repository; run `metareview fsm init`' whenever every listed run carries a non-empty Error summary. The repository may hold many runs; the operator is told none exist and pointed at init instead of at --run or the failed runs.

evidence.note: The CodeNoRuns return is reached both when store.List() is empty and when every summary has s.Error != "".

findings.note: Comment contradicts behaviour on the 'max' effort. The new test's header comment (and internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:133-138) state that claude-opus-4-5/4-6 and claude-sonnet-4-6 'support max but predate xhigh', yet the HTTP effort vocabulary at internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:101 is {low, medium, high, xhigh}, so Preflight rejects max for every HTTP model. The test itself asserts the rejection, so the code is right and only the prose misleads a future reader into thinking max is accepted.
